title: PI Panic
subtitle: Distributed alert and monitoring system for networked devices
description: A distributed alert system designed to monitor device states and trigger escalations based on severity and priority.
Supports real-time communication between nodes and integrates with both UI displays and external systems.
features: Real-time alert and panic escalation system
GUI and optional web interface support
Expandable API for external trigger integration
IO integration for lights, sensors, and external hardware
Device monitoring with online/offline status, last seen, and panic counts
Master web dashboard with device management and active panic monitoring
Optional module bridge for external alert sources
National Weather Service alert monitoring with interactive simulated alert testing
Remote panic and test triggering through ntfy
Client web settings and modular panic monitor management
Client self-panic status and highest-priority locally originated alert display
statusDetails: API layer in development for external triggers
IO integration in progress for hardware interaction
System being refined for usability and expansion
Automatic client restart disabled; network changes require a manual client restart
Client self-panic indicators added for locally originated active alerts and highest-priority local panic; received device panics are excluded
Client web UI reorganized into separate network and monitor pages with master-dashboard styling and improved Connection Key controls
Master web dashboard refresh and panic tracking corrected; active alarms, highest-priority state, and device panic totals now update after received panic events
Web device management implemented with device removal and restoration
Weather optional module and NWS API header standardized; simulated alert testing added
Optional module loading and weather integration still require full end-to-end verification

progressNotes: Initial concept and system design (July 2025)
Designed distributed alert system structure.
Defined panic states, priorities, and message format.
Planned communication model between nodes and master system.
Core communication and backend development (July 2025 to Aug 2025)
Implemented MQTT-based communication system.
Built message handling for panic states and updates.
Established continuous listener and transmit loops.
Alert handling and escalation logic (Aug 2025 to Sep 2025)
Developed priority-based alert system.
Implemented escalation rules for panic conditions.
Standardized event data format across system.
GUI system and display integration (Sep 2025 to Oct 2025)
Built fullscreen GUI for alert display.
Added flashing states and visual indicators.
Integrated dynamic updates from backend events.
System expansion and modular structure (Oct 2025 to Dec 2025)
Refactored system into modular components.
Added support for optional modules and hooks.
Improved reliability and handling of multiple nodes.
Testing, debugging, and stability improvements (Dec 2025 to Jan 2026)
Tested system across multiple nodes and conditions.
Resolved communication edge cases and failures.
Improved reconnection and error handling behavior.
October 2026 development and refinements (Oct 2026)
Added ntfy remote panic and test commands; rate limits still need tuning.
Added device online/offline tracking, last-seen data, persistent panic counts, and master dashboard device removal/restoration.
Corrected master panic processing and dashboard updates; verified active alarms, top panic, and device panic totals during live testing.
Separated master/client web ports to avoid conflicts; saved port settings may require adjustment.
Expanded optional weather module testing with simulated NWS alerts and standardized headers; full driver integration testing remains.
Planned cleanup of shared files, cross-platform paths, user data, settings, and logs; packaging deferred until testing and restructuring.
Added client web network settings and premade/custom panic monitor configuration, with separate monitor pages and modular UI files.
Refined client UI to match master dashboard styling, improve spacing and readability, and provide a wider Connection Key field with compact Show/Hide button.
Disabled automatic client restart after network settings changes; settings save and manual restart remains required.
Added client header self-panic status and top locally originated panic, excluding alarms received from other devices.
